column3: Music spring wire: round, cold-drawn, high-carbon steel wire with a bright smooth finish (Table I: C 0.70-1.00, Mn 0.20-0.60, Si 0.12-0.30, P 0.025 max, S 0.03 max percent)
column4: Federal Specification QQ-W-470B Table II, minimum tensile strength: a procurement requirement every accepted lot must meet, so a guaranteed minimum, not a measured mean
column5: The minimum column of the 25 rows from 0.020 to 0.095 in is transcribed (pages 2-3 of the scan, read at 240 and 400 dpi; every digit fixed by the print, and the strictly decreasing column agrees). Rows 0.004-0.018 and 0.100-0.250 in are left out: piano cores do not need them and some of their 3/8 glyphs are ambiguous in the scan. The maximum column is not transcribed. Inches times 25.4 give millimetres, kips/in2 times 6.894757293168 give MPa. Between rows the claim interpolates linearly in diameter (a declared rule, not the specification's); outside 0.508-2.413 mm it says nothing. Admitted at T = 293.15 K: the specification states no test temperature
